newsitem.title: SPAIN: SOCCER-RONALDO AND ROBSON UNDER FIRE AT BARCELONA.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-RONALDO AND ROBSON UNDER FIRE AT BARCELONA.

text.p: The year cannot end soon enough for Barcelona fans, who have seen their team lose their way as Brazilian international Ronaldo's form dipped in the past few weeks.
Supporters at Sunday's game with Celta Vigo jeered the young striker who until recently had looked set to steamroller his way single-handedly to the Spanish title.
"People who want to whistle should stay at home," he said.
Ronaldo hasn't scored for four games after clocking up 13 goals in as many matches in a whirlwind arrival in the Spanish league which stunned supporters and opponents alike.
Despite his poor performance Barcelona squeezed home 1-0 over Celta and are within two points of arch-rivals Real Madrid.
But even the most ardent Barca fans are now doubting that Bobby Robson's side can last the distance and end a two-season trophy drought at the Camp Nou.
The 2-0 defeat at Real Madrid two weeks ago has proved a major psychological blow, not least because it exploded the aura of invincibility surrounding Ronaldo.
The man the Spanish press compare to Pele missed a simple chance that confirmed he is not at his best in the penalty area.
By contrast Real are riding high thanks to the killer instinct of Croatian international Davor Suker, who overtook Ronaldo in the Spanish goalscoring table at the weekend.
Robson has moved to defend his star player.
"I can understand that the fans are a bit disappointed," said Robson, "But Ronaldo shouldn't be subject to so much pressure."
For the former England manager the result of Sunday's match was the only high note in what he called a 'black week'.
Previously Albert Ferrer announced that he was considering an offer from Real Madrid and hit out at the Barcelona board for paying foreigners more than former reserve-team players.
But the defender was put in his place in no uncertain terms by club president Jose Luis Nunez, and dropped by Robson.
Fans angry at the sidelining of local players such as Ferrer spray-painted insults against Robson and Nunez on the walls of the Camp Nou stadium.
Other supporters were wrestled to the ground by security guards at a midweek training sesssion.
Former coach Johan Cruyff added to the problems by beginning legal action for defamation against Nunez for remarks made when the Dutchman was fired in May.
Many critics feel the move was deliberately timed to disrupt the club.

Robson's problems have inevitably brought the first calls for the return of Cruyff, who won four successive league titles and gave Barcelona their first-ever European Cup in eight years in charge at the Camp Nou.

In a bid to turn around the situation, the Englishman has signed winger Emmanuel Amunike from Sporting Lisbon and will change penalty-taker after Gheorghe Popescu missed from the spot for the second time this season on Sunday.
But Robson may yet lose one of his most influential players in another transfer deal, as Premier League side Middlesborough have increased their offer for defender Miguel Angel Nadal.

"They've offered a lot of money for Nadal, but I don't know if Barcelona will accept the offer, or if it interests Nadal," said Robson who mixes English, Catalan, Portuguese and even some Spanish in his press conferences.
The coach's linguistic potpourri has failed to impress Spanish fans.
One television presenter asked any viewer who had understood what Robson was saying in a press conference to phone the station with a translation.
